"
        },
        {
          "sentence_id": "sent-0004",
          "text": "This ability to combine executable code and descriptive text in a single document has close ties to Knuth’s notion of “literate programming” [ 9 ] and has convinced many researchers to switch to computational notebooks from other programming environments. "

          "sentence_id": "sent-0005",
          "text": "Jupyter Notebooks in particular have seen widespread adoption: as of December 2018, there were more than 3 million Jupyter Notebooks shared publicly on GitHub ( https://www.github.com ) [ 10 ], many of which document academic research [ 11 ]."

      "snapshot": "published",
      "heading": "Introduction",
      "sentence_index": [
        {
          "sentence_id": "sent-0006",
          "text": "The interactive and narrative nature of computational notebooks presents unique opportunities for performing and sharing computational research. "
        },
        {
          "sentence_id": "sent-0007",
          "text": "With some forethought, they can provide not only richly detailed descriptions of analyses but also interactive computing environments for replicating, exploring, and extending them. "

          "sentence_id": "sent-0008",
          "text": "Yet, as with other computing environments, using notebooks for research requires special care. "
        },
        {
          "sentence_id": "sent-0009",
          "text": "Interactively running and editing code in notebooks can delete key steps or introduce “hidden state” that confounds analyses and confuses readers [ 12 ]. "
        },
        {
          "sentence_id": "sent-0010",
          "text": "Analyses documented in notebooks cannot be easily rerun if users do not first freeze their dependencies, share their data, and adequately describe their computing environment [ 13 ]. "
        },
        {
          "sentence_id": "sent-0011",
          "text": "And many notebooks lack sufficient descriptive text to guide readers in using them [ 11 , 14 ]."
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "block_id": "P2-S01-p04",
      "doc_id": "P2",
      "snapshot": "published",
      "heading": "Introduction",
      "sentence_index": [
        {
          "sentence_id": "sent-0012",
          "text": "The explosive growth of computational notebooks provides a unique opportunity to support computational research, but care must be taken when performing and sharing analyses in notebooks. "
        },
        {
          "sentence_id": "sent-0013",
          "text": "Given these opportunities and challenges, we have compiled a set of rules, tips, tools, and example notebooks to help guide Jupyter Notebook authors. "
        },
        {
          "sentence_id": "sent-0014",
          "text": "While we focus on a few core uses of Jupyter Notebooks observed in our own research, many of these rules can be applied to other computational notebooks and use cases. "
        },
        {
          "sentence_id": "sent-0015",
          "text": "In Fig 1 , we give a preview of the rules applied at different phases of the notebook development cycle. "
        },
        {
          "sentence_id": "sent-0016",
          "text": "Whether you use notebooks to track preliminary analyses, to present polished results to collaborators, as finely tuned pipelines for recurring analyses, or for all of the above, following this advice will help you write and share analyses that are easier to read, run, and explore."
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "block_id": "P2-S08-p01",
      "doc_id": "P2",
      "snapshot": "published",
      "heading": "Rule 7: Build a pipeline",
      "sentence_index": [
        {
          "sentence_id": "sent-0017",
          "text": "Notebooks documenting initial, exploratory investigations will rarely be widely generalizable, but once a stable analysis approach has been identified, a well-designed notebook can be generalized into a pipeline that easily repeats that analysis using different input data and parameters. "
        },
        {
          "sentence_id": "sent-0018",
          "text": "With this end in mind, design your notebook from the beginning to allow such future repurposing. "
        },
        {
          "sentence_id": "sent-0019",
          "text": "Place key variable declarations, especially those that will be changed when doing a new analysis, at the top of the notebook rather than burying them somewhere in the middle. "
        },
        {
          "sentence_id": "sent-0020",
          "text": "Perform preparatory steps, like data cleaning, directly in the notebook and avoid manual interventions."
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "block_id": "P2-S08-p02",
      "doc_id": "P2",
      "snapshot": "published",
      "heading": "Rule 7: Build a pipeline",
      "sentence_index": [
        {
          "sentence_id": "sent-0021",
          "text": "Because notebooks’ interactivity make them vulnerable to accidental overwriting or deletion of critical steps by the user, if your analysis runs quickly, make a habit of regularly restarting your kernel and rerunning all cells to make sure you did not accidentally delete a step while cleaning your notebook (and if you did, retrieve the code for it from version control). "
        },
        {
          "sentence_id": "sent-0022",
          "text": "Restarting your kernel and running all cells is also a good final test of results. "
        },
        {
          "sentence_id": "sent-0023",
          "text": "To allow partial execution of complex analyses, break long notebooks into smaller notebooks that focus on one or a few analysis steps. "
        },
        {
          "sentence_id": "sent-0024",
          "text": "Then, ensure that each notebook stores serialized versions of key intermediate results to disk for subsequent notebooks to use."
        }
      ]
    },

      "block_id": "P2-S08-p03",
      "doc_id": "P2",
      "snapshot": "published",
      "heading": "Rule 7: Build a pipeline",
      "sentence_index": [
        {
          "sentence_id": "sent-0025",
          "text": "Once a notebook has been developed, it can be parameterized with a tool such as papermill ( https://github.com/nteract/papermill ). "
        },
        {
          "sentence_id": "sent-0026",
          "text": "Such notebooks can be used not only interactively but also as command-line tools that can be executed automatically—a great boon for pipelines! "
        },
        {
          "sentence_id": "sent-0027",
          "text": "Consider linking your analysis pipeline steps via a Makefile or similar tool that allows for complete noninteractive execution of the entire pipeline, either in full or partial steps. "
        },
        {
          "sentence_id": "sent-0028",
          "text": "Such automation also supports code quality techniques like software testing; consider testing your workflows from end to end each time a change is committed by integrating your repository to a Continuous Integration system (for example, https://travis-ci.org/ ). "
        },
        {
          "sentence_id": "sent-0029",
          "text": "Last but not least, be aware that pipeline notebooks will almost certainly have a very different story (Rule 1) than the initial analyses that engendered them! "
        },
        {
          "sentence_id": "sent-0030",
          "text": "Remember to remove any introduction, interpretation, or conclusion text that is not universally applicable to different inputs and results and instead replace it with guidance for the pipeline user on how to run and interpret its (potentially novel) results."
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "claim": "对运行较快的Notebook，重启内核并从头运行全部单元是发现隐藏状态或遗漏步骤的一种检查办法。"
}<|im_end|>
